claims.content: The Customer wants to browse products by category (gemstones, jewelry, watches, jeweler supplies, and collectibles) or search active auction items using attributes such as product ID, category, type, stone/metal type, price, or full-text description, and view the resulting product listings.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to browse products by category (gemstones, jewelry, watches, jeweler supplies, and collectibles) or search active auction items using attributes such as product ID, category, type, stone/metal type, price, or full-text description, and view the resulting product listings.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer selects a product category or enters search criteria; the system displays the matching active auction items; the Customer views the product listings.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer begins from a product browsing/search interface with category options and a search capability.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The system displays a list of active auction items matching the selected category or search criteria.
in_scope_actions: Browse products by category (gemstones, jewelry, watches, jeweler supplies, collectibles)
Search active auction items by attributes (product ID, category, type, stone/metal type, price, full-text description)
excluded_adjacent_actions: Auction Administration search by Product ID or Customer Email Address
Bidding, checkout, or other downstream purchase actions
variant_dimensions: Browsing a category vs. viewing search results

claims.content: Customer
The system contains active auction items available for browsing and searching.

The Customer triggers the use case by selecting a top-level product category (e.g., jewelry, gemstones, watches) or by entering a keyword or item number into the search field and clicking SEARCH, or by clicking a canned search button (such as Hot Items or Newly Listed).

The Customer selects a top-level product category (e.g., jewelry, gemstones, watches, jeweler supplies, collectibles) from the navigation menu or Site Map, enters search criteria (e.g., keyword, item number, product ID, category, type, stone/metal type, price, or full-text description) and clicks SEARCH, or clicks a canned search button (e.g., Hot Items, Newly Listed).

The system displays a category/search results page containing the matching active auction items; when multiple items are found, it uses the default catalog view, and all listed items include a thumbnail image.
The Customer reviews the product listings using the available display, sort, and pagination controls (Catalog/List View, Sort by, Items Per Page, Go To Page, Previous/Next).
The Customer selects an item from the category/search results to view its details.

The system displays the Product Details Page for the selected item, including the Product Title/Short Description, Product Description/Specifications (up to 1000 characters), other product attribute fields based on product type, and a Product Image with larger-view capability and thumbnails if multiple images exist.
The Customer views the Product Details Page, which includes navigation aids such as the breadcrumb trail, Back to List of Auctions, and Recently Viewed Items.

Diverges from Step 2: If the selected category link or search criteria has no matching product (e.g., a collectibles link with no active auction items), the system displays a 'no results found' page rather than an error or a product listing page.

Diverges from Step 2: If the search returns exactly one matching active auction item, the system loads that item's Product Details Page directly instead of displaying a category/search result listing page.

Diverges from Step 2: If the Customer's search returns no matching active auction items (e.g., searching for 'belly button'), the system displays a 'No Results Found' page instead of a product listing page. This page includes Search Tips, Popular Searches links (static lists for gemstones and jewelry), dynamically updated popular search terms based on Omniture data, and options to try the search again or contact support via phone or email. Exit: if the Customer retries the search or selects a popular search link, return to Step 1; if the Customer contacts support, the use case terminates.

Diverges from Step 4: If the Customer is not signed in and clicks a product module/link in the category/search results to view its details, the system interrupts the flow and presents a sign-in page. After the Customer completes sign-in, the system delivers the Customer to the Product Details page for that product. Exit: proceed to Step 5 after successful sign-in.

Diverges from Step 2: If a product would otherwise match the selected category or search criteria but has no available image to display, the product is not eligible to appear on a catalog page, in search results, or on a product details page; the system omits it from the displayed listings. Exit: the use case continues at Step 2 with the remaining matching active auction items.

After the Customer selects an item from the listings, the system displays the Product Details Page with the product title/short description, full description/specifications (up to 1000 characters), type-specific attribute fields, visible Gemstone Treatment field for gemstone-containing products, product image with enlargement and thumbnails, Item Product ID (SKU), and navigation aids including breadcrumb trail, Back to List of Auctions, and Recently Viewed Items strip.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] Main Flow step 1 repeats the Trigger's initiating action (selecting a category, entering search criteria, clicking SEARCH/canned search) rather than starting after the Trigger. After the Customer has already triggered the use case, the first Main Flow step should advance to the system's response, so step 1 should be removed/merged and the results display should become the first step.

inconsistency_hints: Main Flow goes beyond the listing results page: step 2 displays the listing page, but steps 4-6 continue to selection and display/viewing of the Product Details Page. Postconditions claim 0 states as a final postcondition that the system displays the product listing page, which is no longer the displayed state at the end of the main flow; it describes an intermediate state, not the final reachable state.

Postconditions claim 0 describes an intermediate listing page that is already reached at Main Flow step 2, before the Customer selects an item. The last Main Flow step ends with the Customer viewing the Product Details Page, so this intermediate state cannot be a postcondition of the completed flow; the postconditions slot mixes a mid-flow milestone with the final outcome.
